statement: Lower birthweight / impaired fetal growth is associated with higher adult coronary heart disease, hypertension, stroke and type 2 diabetes (the Barker / developmental-origins / DOHaD hypothesis).
effect_size: Inverse gradient of birthweight with adult cardiometabolic disease across multiple cohorts; reverses interpretation of disease as purely adult-lifestyle-driven
population: Historical birth cohorts (Hertfordshire, south India, others); ecological + individual epidemiology

provenance.primary: Barker DJP et al., 'Fetal growth and coronary heart disease in south India', Lancet 1996; reviewed in Gluckman, Hanson, Cooper & Thornburg, NEJM 2008
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave life-stages brief; PubMed E-utilities verified (PMID 18596274, 8909379)

confidence_notes: Strong, replicated, mechanistically coherent but fundamentally OBSERVATIONAL (cannot randomize a fetus). Birthweight is a predictor, not a fixed sentence; adult lifestyle still moves the same risks. Value is upstream/population-level.

statement: Fetal undernutrition reprograms metabolism toward fuel-sparing (fewer beta-cells, more insulin resistance); adaptive in a scarce later environment, but a liability ('predictive adaptive mismatch') in a calorie-rich one, raising type 2 diabetes risk.
effect_size: Mechanistic model explaining the birthweight-diabetes association
population: Human cohorts + animal models; Dutch Hunger Winter natural experiment

provenance.primary: Hales CN & Barker DJP, 'Type 2 (non-insulin-dependent) diabetes mellitus: the thrifty phenotype hypothesis', Diabetologia 1992

confidence_notes: Mechanism claim; must not be presented as a confirmed adult OUTCOME for an individual. The thrifty-genotype vs thrifty-phenotype debate is ongoing.

statement: Prenatal exposure to the time-limited Dutch Hunger Winter famine (1944-45) is associated with altered adult metabolic, cardiovascular and late-life brain outcomes 60-70+ years later, with effects dependent on gestational timing of exposure and some epigenetic (DNA-methylation) signatures.
effect_size: Timing-dependent effects (early-gestation: obesity/lipids/CVD; late-gestation: glucose intolerance); persistent methylation differences (e.g. IGF2)
population: Dutch famine birth cohort, longitudinal follow-up (Roseboom and colleagues)

provenance.primary: Roseboom TJ et al., Dutch Hunger Winter cohort program; recent late-life brain analyses Neuroimage 2025 / Brain Res 2025

confidence_notes: Strongest quasi-causal evidence for DOHaD (well-documented, time-limited exposure on a previously well-nourished population). Still observational at the individual level.

statement: Periconceptional folic acid supplementation markedly reduces neural-tube-defect risk (~72% reduction in recurrence in the MRC RCT); must begin before conception because the neural tube closes by ~week 4.
effect_size: ~72% relative reduction in NTD recurrence
population: MRC Vitamin Study RCT, women at high recurrence risk; basis for population flour fortification

provenance.primary: MRC Vitamin Study Research Group, 'Prevention of neural tube defects: results of the Medical Research Council Vitamin Study', Lancet 1991

confidence_notes: RCT-grade, the best-evidenced perinatal supplement. Timing is load-bearing: must start pre-conception, which is why fortification works.

statement: Maternal iodine deficiency impairs fetal brain development; even mild-to-moderate deficiency in a developed-country population is associated with lower child IQ and reading ability. Iodine deficiency is the leading preventable cause of intellectual impairment worldwide.
effect_size: Lower verbal IQ and reading scores in children of mildly iodine-deficient mothers (ALSPAC); large effects from overt deficiency globally
population: ALSPAC UK pregnancy cohort (mild deficiency); global public-health data (overt)

provenance.primary: Bath SC et al., 'Effect of inadequate iodine status in UK pregnant women on cognitive outcomes in their children (ALSPAC)', Lancet 2013

confidence_notes: Mild-deficiency evidence is cohort (residual confounding possible); overt-deficiency causation is established public-health/RCT. Deficiency-correction lever, not a mega-dose-better story.

statement: Omega-3 (DHA/EPA) supplementation in pregnancy modestly reduces preterm and early-preterm birth and low birthweight; the marketed cognitive ('smarter baby') benefit is not robustly supported.
effect_size: Reduced preterm (<37wk) and early preterm (<34wk) birth; cognition endpoints inconsistent
population: Cochrane review of 70 RCTs (~20,000 women)

provenance.primary: Middleton P et al., 'Omega-3 fatty acid addition during pregnancy', Cochrane Database Syst Rev 2018

confidence_notes: Real but modest for preterm birth (meta/strong); 'smarter baby' cognitive claim is mixed/overstated relative to the marketing.

statement: For uncomplicated pregnancies, regular moderate exercise is safe and beneficial (reduces gestational diabetes and excessive weight gain, likely reduces pre-eclampsia and cesarean) without increasing preterm birth - refuting the old 'rest, don't exert' advice.
effect_size: Lower GDM and excess gestational weight gain; no increase in adverse fetal outcomes
population: Meta-analyses + obstetric guideline consensus (ACOG and equivalents)

provenance.primary: ACOG and international obstetric guideline consensus on physical activity in pregnancy; supporting meta-analyses

confidence_notes: Applies to UNCOMPLICATED pregnancy; specific precautions (supine late, contact sports, overheating, high-risk obstetric conditions) apply. Folklore (rest) refuted by evidence (activity).

statement: Treating gestational diabetes (diet, glucose monitoring, insulin as needed) reduces serious perinatal complications, establishing that screening and treatment are worthwhile.
effect_size: Reduced serious perinatal outcomes (death, shoulder dystocia, fractures, nerve palsy) vs routine care
population: ACHOIS RCT, n=1000 women with GDM

provenance.primary: Crowther CA et al., 'Effect of treatment of gestational diabetes mellitus on pregnancy outcomes', NEJM 2005

confidence_notes: RCT-grade. GDM also carries a DOHaD link to the child's later metabolic risk.

statement: Low-dose aspirin started in the first trimester in screened high-risk women markedly reduces preterm pre-eclampsia.
effect_size: ~62% reduction in preterm pre-eclampsia vs placebo (ASPRE)
population: ASPRE RCT, ~1620 high-risk women identified by first-trimester screening

provenance.primary: Rolnik DL et al., 'Aspirin versus Placebo in Pregnancies at High Risk for Preterm Preeclampsia', NEJM 2017
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave life-stages brief; companion AJOG analyses PubMed-verified (PMID 28888591)

confidence_notes: RCT-grade; now standard guideline care. DOI from author knowledge; companion trial papers verified on PubMed.

statement: Female fertility declines with age - gradually from the late 20s, more steeply after ~35 and sharply after ~40 - driven primarily by declining oocyte QUALITY (aneuploidy), not just quantity; the egg pool is fixed at birth and non-renewing.
effect_size: Per-cycle conception probability and fertile-window duration both decline with age
population: Prospective fecundability studies (Dunson et al.)

provenance.primary: Dunson DB et al., 'Changes with age in the level and duration of fertility in the menstrual cycle', Human Reproduction 2002

confidence_notes: Strong, replicated. The dominant fertility lever and the one no supplement moves - a predictor that is also near-destiny.

statement: Male fertility also declines with age (later and more gradually than female): sperm count, motility and especially DNA integrity worsen with paternal age, and advanced paternal age is associated with modestly higher rates of some offspring conditions.
effect_size: Rising sperm DNA fragmentation (SCSA) with age across large clinic series
population: Large infertility-clinic cohorts (e.g. 25,445 men, SCSA)

provenance.primary: Evenson DP et al., sperm chromatin structure assay vs age, Fertility & Sterility 2020

confidence_notes: 'Men can father at any age' is half-true: possible, but with rising sperm-quality and offspring-risk caveats.

statement: Elective oocyte vitrification (egg freezing) is a real but probabilistic fertility-preservation option, not a guarantee; outcomes depend heavily on age at freezing (younger better) and number of eggs stored, and many women who freeze never use them.
effect_size: Live-birth probability rises with more eggs and younger freezing age; substantial non-return rate
population: Large vitrification registry/clinic series (Cobo et al.)

provenance.primary: Cobo A et al., 'Oocyte vitrification for fertility preservation for both medical and nonmedical reasons', Fertility & Sterility 2021

confidence_notes: Technology works; honest counseling is in probabilities and egg-counts, not promises. IVF success overall is dominated by egg age (donor-egg cycles erase recipient age effect).

statement: Antioxidant/fertility supplements for subfertility (female and male) have low-quality evidence and no reliable demonstrated benefit on live birth - the fertility-supplement industry is sold with far more confidence than the trials support.
effect_size: No reliable effect on live birth; evidence graded low / very low certainty
population: Cochrane reviews of antioxidant RCTs in subfertile women and men

provenance.primary: Showell MG et al., 'Antioxidants for female subfertility', Cochrane 2020 (CD007807.pub4); de Ligny W et al., 'Antioxidants for male subfertility', Cochrane 2022 (CD007411.pub5)

confidence_notes: Meta-tier but LOW certainty / largely null. CoQ10/DHEA/inositol have small context-specific signals (e.g. inositol in PCOS) but are not general 'fertility boosters'. Predictor-vs-lever: hopeful mechanism != proven outcome.

statement: ~90% of adult bone mass is laid down by ~age 18-20 and peak bone mass is reached by the late 20s; weight-bearing/impact exercise, adequate calcium and vitamin D, and avoiding smoking/under-fueling in youth build a higher peak and more margin before the later fracture threshold.
effect_size: Childhood/adolescent loading raises peak BMD; the asset later aging/menopause spends
population: Systematic review / National Osteoporosis Foundation position statement

provenance.primary: Weaver CM et al., 'The National Osteoporosis Foundation's position statement on peak bone mass development and lifestyle factors', Osteoporos Int 2016

confidence_notes: Strong. The 'build the account' foundation; cross-ref the menopausal bone-loss slope (Domain N / section 13) that draws it down.

statement: The adolescent brain matures unevenly: the limbic/reward system matures early (driving sensation-seeking) while the prefrontal cortex (judgment, impulse control, planning) matures last, into the mid-20s - a developmental mismatch that is the neurobiological basis of elevated adolescent risk-taking.
effect_size: Earlier limbic vs later prefrontal maturation gap
population: Developmental neuroscience (neuroimaging + behavioral)

provenance.primary: Steinberg L and developmental-neuroscience literature on dual-systems adolescent brain maturation
provenance.surfaced_via: Wave life-stages brief; developmental neuroscience synthesis

confidence_notes: Mechanistic/cohort; a stage, not a defect. Practical reading: adolescents need scaffolding (structure, sleep, guardrails) while internal regulators are still wiring.

statement: Screen time is consistently associated with worse sleep (later bedtimes, shorter duration) in children and adolescents; combined with the pubertal circadian phase-delay, this is the strongest argument for protecting teen sleep and later school start times.
effect_size: Adverse screen-sleep association in the majority of reviewed studies
population: Systematic review of school-aged children and adolescents

provenance.primary: Hale L & Guan S, 'Screen time and sleep among school-aged children and adolescents: a systematic literature review', Sleep Med Rev 2015

confidence_notes: Largely correlational and partly bidirectional, but consistent and mechanistically plausible (displacement + light + arousal). Low-risk lever; the pubertal melatonin phase-delay is independently established (cross-ref Domain I).

statement: Frailty is a distinct, measurable state of diminished physiological reserve (>=3 of 5: unintentional weight loss, exhaustion, weakness/low grip, slow gait, low activity) that predicts falls, hospitalization, disability and death - separate from age or comorbidity alone.
effect_size: Frailty phenotype predicts adverse outcomes; pre-frail (1-2 criteria) is an intervention window
population: Cardiovascular Health Study (>5000 older adults)

provenance.primary: Fried LP et al., 'Frailty in older adults: evidence for a phenotype', J Gerontol A Biol Sci Med Sci 2001

confidence_notes: Foundational cohort. A powerful PREDICTOR (readout of reserve), not a single lever; the modifiable core is sarcopenia (resistance/power/protein). Complements the deficit-accumulation Frailty Index (Rockwood).

statement: In older adults, accumulated medications become a leading cause of harm (falls, confusion, hospitalization, interactions); supervised deprescribing - planned reduction/stopping of drugs whose harms now outweigh benefits - is a recognized, evidence-informed clinical discipline.
effect_size: Reduced medication burden and drug-related harm; tools = STOPP/START, Beers criteria
population: Geriatric clinical literature; deprescribing-process guidance and growing RCT base

provenance.primary: Scott IA et al., 'Reducing inappropriate polypharmacy: the process of deprescribing', JAMA Internal Medicine 2015

confidence_notes: The geriatric inversion of 'predictor != lever': sometimes the lever is REMOVING a thing. Deprescribing RCTs are growing and broadly favorable for specific drug classes; harm-reduction is well established.

statement: If the onset of chronic disability can be postponed faster than the age of death advances, the period of end-of-life morbidity is compressed into a shorter window - more healthy years, fewer years of decline ('compression of morbidity'). This is the rigorous statement of healthspan>lifespan.
effect_size: Conceptual target ('squaring the curve'); component levers individually evidence-graded
population: Population health theory (Fries)

provenance.primary: Fries JF, 'Aging, natural death, and the compression of morbidity', NEJM 1980

confidence_notes: Hypothesis/framework (theoretical-cohort), debated empirically (does morbidity actually compress?). The COMPONENTS (exercise, deprescribing, falls prevention) are individually graded across the manual.

statement: Early integration of palliative care alongside standard oncology improved quality of life and mood, reduced aggressive end-of-life treatment, AND was associated with longer survival - palliative care is symptom-and-meaning-focused care, not the abandonment of care.
effect_size: Better QoL/mood, less aggressive EOL care, and longer median survival vs standard care
population: RCT, metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer patients (n=151)

provenance.primary: Temel JS et al., 'Early palliative care for patients with metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer', NEJM 2010

confidence_notes: RCT-grade and counter-intuitive: more comfort-focused care delivered BOTH better quality and (at least non-inferior, here superior) survival. Corrects the 'palliative = giving up' misconception.

statement: Advance care planning (living will + designated healthcare proxy) in elderly patients improves end-of-life care, makes it more likely patients' wishes are known and followed, and reduces stress, anxiety and depression in surviving relatives.
effect_size: Wishes more often known/followed; higher patient+family satisfaction; lower relative bereavement distress
population: RCT, elderly inpatients (n=309)

provenance.primary: Detering KM et al., 'The impact of advance care planning on end of life care in elderly patients: randomised controlled trial', BMJ 2010

confidence_notes: RCT-supports. A high-value, low-cost, evidence-backed intervention most people defer until too late.
